1. Exact theorem and inherited finite-chain modules
---------------------------------------------------
Fix J,tau>0 and kappa>lambda_c/3, lambda_c=2J*pi^2. Set

 lambda=lambda_*(kappa)=inf_{theta!=0}
 [(J/2)int theta'^2-kappa int rho^2]/int rho,
 theta in H^1_0(0,1),0<=theta<=pi, rho=sin^2(theta/2).

The previously audited classical sine trial gives lambda<lambda_c.
There are S=L-1 spin sites, BOTH endpoint fields, and

 Hcrit=J sum_{i=1}^{S-1}(I-sigma_i dot sigma_{i+1})
                        +J(I-Z_1)+J(I-Z_S),
 A_L=L^2 Hcrit, N=sum n_i, W=sum n_i n_{i+1},
 B_L=A_L-kappa W-lambda N, Z_L=Tr exp(-tau B_L).

Thus physical V_L=-4J-kappa/L^2 and beta=tau L^2. All spin sectors
are retained. N COMMUTES with B_L. No eigenbasis or Gibbs sampler is
supplied. The inherited contact/cube/trace modules are spelled out in
Section6; the macroscopic trial lower bound itself does not use the
matching Gamma-liminf or a full partition upper bound.

Main claim. There are eps>0 and c,C,L0>0, depending on the fixed
parameters, such that for L>=L0,

 Tr_{N>floor(eps L)} exp(-tau B_L)>=c sqrt(L),             (1.1)
 Tr_{N<=floor(eps L)} exp(-tau B_L)->Z_B(tau,lambda)<infinity,
 Z_B=product_{j>=1}[1-exp(tau(lambda-2J*pi^2*j^2))]^{-1}, (1.2)
 Pr_L(N<=floor(eps L))<=C/sqrt(L)->0.                    (1.3)

In particular Z_L diverges, every fixed number cutoff loses ALL mass,
and the family is not particle-number tight. On any number-preserving
common Fock embedding its half-trace distance from the ideal Bose state
at lambda tends to1. This is stronger than merely failure of equality
of the partition. It does not determine Z_L/sqrt(L), a particular
nonzero profile, or a mixed macroscopic law's weights.

2. Nonzero coexistence minimizer exists and is smooth
-----------------------------------------------------
The quotient is bounded below by lambda_c-kappa: Poincare and
theta^2>=4rho give (J/2)int theta'^2>=lambda_c int rho, while rho^2<=rho.
Take a quotient-minimizing sequence theta_j. Its quotient Q_j is bounded
above and its derivative energy satisfies
(J/2)int theta_j'^2=Q_j int rho_j+kappa int rho_j^2
                                  <=(Q_j+kappa)int rho_j.
Thus it is H^1-bounded and has a uniformly convergent subsequence.

The limit cannot be zero. If it were, sup rho_j->0, whereas
Q_j>=lambda_c-kappa sup rho_j would give liminf Q_j>=lambda_c,
contradicting lambda_*<lambda_c. Th
